summary: Build and debug real Arduino circuits in a free browser simulator, from your first blinking LED to sensors, motors, state machines, and a working robot.
description: Every circuit in this course runs on a simulated Arduino Uno in Wokwi, a free in-browser simulator, so you can wire LEDs, buttons, potentiometers, light and temperature sensors, servos, and motors without buying parts or risking damage. You write real Arduino C++ (the same code runs unchanged on a physical Uno), and you check the electrical math first with short Python programs that show their real output and charts on the page: Ohm's law, LED resistor sizing, voltage dividers, and ADC conversions. Each module has notes that teach the ideas, a build-along that makes one working project step by step, and a practice set with hints and full solutions. Later modules drive motors safely through a driver, organize robot behavior as state machines with feedback, test robots under changing conditions, and finish with an obstacle-avoiding or line-following robot capstone. Tinkercad Circuits works as a backup simulator, and an optional starter kit lets you build everything for real with Arduino IDE 2.
audience: Teens and beginners who have written a few programs with conditions and loops, and want to understand circuits, sensors, motors, and how robots make decisions.
prerequisites: Write simple programs with variables, if/else, and loops (in any language)
Comfortable using a web browser and copying text between windows
outcomes: Apply Ohm's law and power calculations to size resistors and keep circuits within safe current and heat limits.
Lay out breadboard circuits with LEDs, buttons, and potentiometers, and find wiring faults by tracing nodes.
Read digital and analog sensors, convert raw readings to volts and real units, and smooth noisy signals.
Drive servos and DC motors safely through a motor driver with a separate power supply.
Organize robot behavior as a state machine with feedback, and test it under varied conditions.
Build, test, and present a simulated or physical obstacle-avoiding or line-following robot.

primaryTool.name: Wokwi (free Arduino simulator in the browser)
primaryTool.description: Wokwi simulates an Arduino Uno together with LEDs, resistors, buttons, potentiometers, sensors, servos, and more, right in a web browser. Nothing to install, nothing to buy, and nothing can burn out, so you can test every circuit before touching real parts. A free account is only needed to save projects online.
setupSteps: Open wokwi.com in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari.
Click the Arduino (Uno, Mega, Nano) tile, then choose Arduino Uno under Start from Scratch.
Paste the lesson's code into sketch.ino and, when given, its circuit into diagram.json.
Press the green play button to compile and run the simulation.
primaryTool.verification: The official Blink project runs and the small L LED on the simulated Uno blinks about once per second.

optionalGear.name: Arduino Uno starter kit
optionalGear.description: Optional. A Uno (or compatible) board with a USB cable, breadboard, LEDs, resistors, buttons, and a potentiometer lets you build Modules 2 to 4 for real. Wokwi covers every lesson without it.

optionalGear.name: Extra sensors
optionalGear.description: Optional. A photoresistor, a TMP36 temperature sensor, an ultrasonic distance sensor, or a soil moisture probe for building the sensor projects on a desk.

optionalGear.name: 2WD robot chassis kit
optionalGear.description: Optional. A small chassis with two DC motors and wheels for building the capstone robot physically. Most kits also need a motor driver board and a AA battery pack.

freeCompletionPromise: Every lesson can be finished for $0 in a web browser: circuits run in Wokwi's free simulator without an account, and the Python calculations show their output right on the lesson page. Hardware is optional, and no lesson requires buying anything.

assignments.title: Sensor and button panel
assignments.brief: Wire a pushbutton, a potentiometer, and a light or temperature sensor in Wokwi, then debounce the button, convert and smooth the sensor readings, and switch LEDs on thresholds using millis() timers instead of delay().

assignments.title: Motor controller with a state machine
assignments.brief: Build a Wokwi controller that drives a motor through driver signals with a speed ramp and a stop button, and runs a state machine with millis() timers, such as a sliding door that reverses when something blocks it.

capstone.title: Obstacle-avoiding or line-following robot
capstone.brief: Build a robot in Wokwi, or on a real chassis, that avoids obstacles or follows a line, with filtered sensor readings, motor control through driver signals, one case per state, and safety features like a stop button and a speed limit.
deliverables: Wokwi project with a circuit diagram and pin plan
State diagram that matches the code
